text: Nobody is sure how big it was. The cameras that should have recorded it were out of focus, or pointed the wrong way, or lost the vehicle altogether. So Rocha asks for a photograph of the wing.

text: He asks on flight day four and gets no answer. He asks again on flight day six. And on the morning of the twenty second, he is told the Shuttle Program is not requesting any outside imaging help.

text: So he writes it down. That this is the wrong answer. That it borders on irresponsible. And at the end, this.

text: Remember the NASA safety posters everywhere around stating, if it's not safe, say so? Yes, it's that serious.
He printed it out, carried it down the hall, and showed it to a colleague. He never sent it. Asked why, he told the accident board he did not want to jump the chain of command.

text: Six months later, in San Antonio, engineers loaded a block of that foam into a nitrogen cannon built for testing bird strikes, and fired it at a shuttle wing at five hundred and thirty miles an hour.

text: This is what it did. A hole roughly sixteen inches across, straight through the leading edge. The photograph Rodney Rocha asked for, three times, was never taken.

text: April, nineteen eighty one. Columbia is the first orbiter, and this is the first flight of the programme. It comes back with damaged tiles.

cap: The first flight. The first damage.

text: The external tank is covered in insulating foam, because it holds liquid hydrogen at two hundred and fifty three degrees below zero and it would otherwise ice over.
videoQuery: external tank insulation foam orange spray application factory

text: The design requirement was explicit. The tank was not supposed to shed anything. Not foam, not ice, nothing.
It shed foam on the first flight. And on the second. And it kept doing it, for twenty two years, on flight after flight after flight.
videoQuery: space shuttle launch ascent external tank separation tracking

text: There is a particular place on the tank called the left bipod ramp, a wedge of hand sprayed foam over the strut that holds the orbiter's nose.
Before Columbia's last flight, foam had come off that exact ramp at least six times.
source: CAIB Report, Vol. I, ch. 6, p. 123

text: But here is the part that matters. At the flight readiness review before Columbia launched, managers were told there had been only three.
source: CAIB Report, Vol. I, ch. 6, p. 125
note: Dim-1 correction #9. Events four and five (STS-52, STS-62) were discovered by the BOARD, after the accident. The people approving the flight rationale were reasoning from a count wrong by half.

text: Two of the six had not been found yet. The accident board discovered them afterwards, going back through the record. The people approving the flight were working from a number that was wrong by half.
videoQuery: nasa engineers meeting conference room briefing slides projector

text: December, nineteen eighty eight. Atlantis comes back from a classified mission with more than seven hundred damaged tiles and one tile missing altogether.

The commander later said he believed they were going to die on re entry. The damage was directly beneath an antenna mounting plate, which was made of steel, and that is the only reason the wing survived.
cap: A steel plate. That is the whole reason.

text: October, two thousand and two. Three months before Columbia. Foam comes off the left bipod ramp and hits the solid rocket booster attach ring, about four inches wide and three inches deep.
videoQuery: solid rocket booster attach hardware closeup launch vehicle

text: That was the closest warning anyone got, and it arrived two missions before the accident. The programme classified it, flew twice more, and did not fix the ramp.
videoQuery: space shuttle vehicle assembly building crawler transport

text: There is a word for what was happening, and the accident board used it. NASA had two categories for problems. In family, and out of family.
source: CAIB Report, Vol. I, ch. 6, p. 122

text: In family meant a problem you had seen before, within the experience base. Out of family meant something new. Foam loss had been seen so many times that it had become, by definition, in family.
videoQuery: documents paperwork filing archive shelves office

text: The board called that a strange term indeed for a violation of system requirements. Because the classification had been introduced after Challenger, to help. And by definition, the problems moved into the lesser category got less attention.
source: CAIB Report, Vol. I, ch. 6, p. 196
cap: A post-Challenger reform. It became a mechanism.

text: The sociologist who worked on this report has a name for it. The normalisation of deviance. You see the thing that should not happen, and it does not kill you, so it stops being the thing that should not happen.

text: On the sixteenth of January, two thousand and three, seven people boarded that orbiter for a sixteen day science mission.
Rick Husband, commander. William McCool, pilot. Michael Anderson, payload commander. Kalpana Chawla, flight engineer. David Brown. Laurel Clark. And Ilan Ramon, the first Israeli in space.
It was not a station flight. There was no docking, no rendezvous. Columbia carried a laboratory module in the payload bay and the crew ran experiments around the clock in two shifts.

cap: SPACEHAB. Around the clock, two shifts.

text: That detail matters more than it sounds. Because Columbia was not going to the space station, it had no robotic arm fitted, and there was nowhere to shelter if anything went wrong.
